_comment: Features merged on main. Claim only what is merged; set "soon": true for work in progress, or "tag" for a short label instead ("Awaiting Google verification"). "highlight": true puts a card on the home page (keep six to eight). Each group's "status" (works, partly or planned) and "status_note" is the one place the site says how far an area is; keep it in step with the README's project status table and ROADMAP.md.

groups.title: Privacy and safety
groups.intro: Mailcrane treats every message as untrusted and keeps what you read to yourself.
groups.status_note: Encrypted mail (OpenPGP and S/MIME) comes later, in milestone M5.

items.title: Trackers blocked
items.text: Tracking pixels and images from 37 known email-tracking services are removed, even when you load images. Each message says how many were blocked and who sent them.

items.title: Remote images off by default
items.text: Pictures stored on the sender's server stay hidden until you tap “Load remote images” for that message. They then load without cookies or a referrer.

items.title: See where a link really goes
items.text: Tapping a link shows its real destination first, and warns when the link text names a different site, uses an IP address, mixes alphabets or isn't secure. Tracking tags such as utm_source are removed before it opens.

items.title: Phishing warnings
items.text: A chip shows whether your provider could confirm the sender (SPF, DKIM and DMARC, in plain words), and a warning appears when a sender's name pretends to be a different address.

items.title: Safe HTML
items.text: Scripts, forms, frames and risky styles are stripped before a message is shown, and hidden text-direction tricks are removed from names, subjects and file names.

items.title: App lock
items.text: Ask for your fingerprint, face or screen lock before your mail shows. While it's on, screenshots and the recent-apps preview are blocked.

items.title: No analytics, no ads
items.text: No tracking, no ads and no Mailcrane servers. Your mail goes only between your phone and your mail server, and passwords stay in Android's secure storage.

groups.title: Accounts
groups.intro: Bring the email address you already have.
groups.status_note: IMAP, SMTP, JMAP and automatic setup are built. Sign in with Google waits for Google to verify the app, and Sign in with Microsoft is planned.

items.title: IMAP and SMTP
items.text: Works with almost any provider. Connections always use TLS with certificate checks, and Mailcrane tests both servers before it saves anything.

items.title: JMAP
items.text: Full support for the modern JMAP protocol used by Fastmail, Stalwart and others: read, act on and send mail like any other account.

items.title: Automatic setup
items.text: Type your address and password and Mailcrane finds the server settings from your provider's own configuration, DNS records or a built-in provider list. Your address is never sent anywhere else.

items.title: Several accounts
items.text: Add as many accounts as you like, each with its own colour and signature. The same account can't be added twice by mistake.

items.title: Gmail sign-in
items.text: Sign in to Gmail with your Google account in the system browser, without an app password. It's built, and waiting for Google to verify the app.

groups.title: Inbox
groups.intro: A fast, calm inbox that works offline.

items.title: Unified inbox
items.text: See every account's inbox together, with a coloured dot for each account, or switch to one account from the drawer.

items.title: Conversations
items.text: Replies are grouped with the message they answer, including your own from the Sent folder. Turn it off if you prefer single messages.

items.title: Instant search, even offline
items.text: Search subjects, people and message text on your phone, accents ignored, with chips for sender, attachments, unread, flagged, date and account.

items.title: Select several
items.text: Long-press to select messages, then mark read, flag, archive, delete or move them all at once, with undo.

items.title: Swipe actions
items.text: Swipe left or right to archive, delete, mark read, flag or move: you choose which.

items.title: Snooze
items.text: Send a message away until later today, tomorrow, the weekend or a time you pick. It comes back unread, with a notification.

items.title: Sender pictures and density
items.text: Initials on a steady colour, or your contacts' photos if you allow it, never images from the internet. Prefer more on screen? Pick Compact.

items.title: Date headers
items.text: Mail is grouped under Today, Yesterday, This week and then by month, in your language.

items.title: Ready offline
items.text: Recent mail downloads in the background (on Wi-Fi by default) so it opens at once, and anything you do offline is sent when you're back.

items.title: Tablets, foldables and widgets
items.text: The list and the message sit side by side on big screens, with keyboard shortcuts, and a home-screen widget shows what's unread.

groups.title: Write
groups.intro: Sending just works, even without a signal.

items.title: Scheduled send and undo send
items.text: Pick when a message goes out, or take it back in the seconds after you tap Send.

items.title: Outbox that never loses mail
items.text: Messages wait in the Outbox while you're offline and are sent as soon as the network is back.

items.title: Formatting, attachments and signatures
items.text: Bold, italic, lists and links, files of any kind, and a signature per account. Drafts save as you type and sync to your other devices.

items.title: Smart recipients
items.text: Suggestions from people you write to, and from your contacts if you allow it.

groups.title: Organise
groups.intro: Keep mail sorted the way you like.

items.title: Folders
items.text: Create, rename, move and delete folders from your phone, on IMAP and JMAP accounts. Every change is made on your server too.

items.title: Rules
items.text: Move, archive, flag or mark mail read by sender, recipient, subject, attachment or mailing list.

items.title: Rules on your server
items.text: If your provider supports ManageSieve, rules run on the server, so mail is sorted even while your phone is off. Your other filters are left alone.

items.title: One-tap unsubscribe
items.text: Newsletters get an Unsubscribe button. Mailcrane tells you how it will unsubscribe before it does.

groups.title: Notifications
groups.status_note: Push wake-ups still need a check on a real phone with a real distributor app.

items.title: New-mail notifications
items.text: One notification per message, with Archive and Mark read buttons. Sender and subject can be hidden with “Hide message content outside the app”.

items.title: Always-on sync
items.text: Optional: new mail arrives within a minute. It reconnects after network changes, reboots and updates by itself.

items.title: UnifiedPush
items.text: Optional wake-ups through a UnifiedPush distributor app, for people who run a push gateway. No Google services needed.

items.title: JMAP push
items.text: Instant new mail from JMAP servers through UnifiedPush, without a separate gateway.

groups.title: Look and feel
groups.intro: Comfortable to read, day and night.
groups.status_note: Dark mode and Material You are built. Translations wait for the Weblate project to open, and a full accessibility review comes before 1.0.

items.title: Dark mode and Material You
items.text: Light, dark or follow the system, with colours from your wallpaper on Android 12 and later. HTML mail stays readable in dark mode.

items.title: Accessible
items.text: Designed for TalkBack and large text. A full accessibility review, including colour contrast, comes before 1.0.

items.title: In your language
items.text: Translations through Weblate, so anyone can help, once the Weblate project opens.
